newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klestil says nothing to hide in Kurd murder case.
newsitem.headline: Klestil says nothing to hide in Kurd murder case.

text.p: Austrian President Thomas Klestil, responding for the first time to allegations he pulled strings to allow suspected Iranian assassins to flee, insisted on Wednesday he had nothing to hide.
"I am in favour of putting all the documents on the table. I have nothing to conceal," Klestil told Austrian news agancy APA as he flew back from an official visit to Spain.
Klestil was a senior official in the foreign ministry in 1989 when Iranian Kurdish leader Abdorrahman Qasemlu and two other activists were slain in a Vienna flat by suspected Iranian hitmen.

"I did not try to influence the decisions of the interior and justice ministries. All those involved know that and the papers prove it," Klestil said, rejecting claims he had exerted pressure on the other two ministries to drop the case.
Former Iranian president Abolhassan Bani-Sadr and a former Austrian diplomat have alleged Austria, fearing retaliation from Iran, allowed two of the three Iranian suspects to flee.
Warrants for their arrest were only issued when they were outside the country.

Opposition parties have called for a parliamentary inquiry into the matter and on May 22 began a 20-day boycott of parliamentary business to protest at the government's use of its parliamentary majority to block their request.

Chancellor Viktor Klima's Social Democrats and junior coalition partner the People's Party have argued a report prepared by the interior, foreign and justice ministries exonerates politicians of any wrong-doing.
Klestil, a member of the conservative People's Party, has yet to say whether he will run for reelection next year.
